best_for: Music collectors on Windows or Mac with large libraries in many formats who want a free player they can tag, convert and reshape to taste.
description:
foobar2000 is a music player written by Peter Pawlowski. Besides the desktop apps there are versions for Android and iOS, and new releases usually go out for all of them at the same time.

You can rearrange the window layout until it shows only what you care about, and set your own keyboard shortcuts. Built-in DSP effects shape the sound as it plays. Internet radio is included, with Radio Browser built in to find stations. On a home network, foobar2000 can stream your music, control network audio players, or act as a remote for another copy of foobar2000 running on a different device. On Linux, the Windows version runs under Wine.

points.title: Free, with no tracking
points.text: foobar2000 is freeware, and its site states there is no telemetry and no data collection. It is not open source.

points.title: Plays it all, without gaps
points.text: Mainstream audio formats play out of the box, with gapless playback and full ReplayGain support. Live albums and DJ mixes run without breaks, at even volume.

points.title: Components add the rest
points.text: Third-party components add decoders, effects and more. Windows can load VST effects and macOS can load Audio Units. The Mac page links a separate list of components that work on macOS, so check it before you switch.

points.title: Rip, convert and tag
points.text: It rips audio CDs, converts between formats and has advanced tag editing. Extra encoders for the converter come in the separate Free Encoder Pack.

points.title: Old PCs still welcome
points.text: The Windows build runs on Windows 7 or newer, in 32-bit, 64-bit and ARM64EC installers that install machine-wide. The Mac app needs macOS 11 or newer and runs on Intel and Apple silicon.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows only
points.text: This site keeps 41 Windows versions. macOS lists only the current universal build; foobar2000 keeps an archive of older Mac releases on its own site.
